scope: current Books 10–16 held-source occurrences; selected and exploratory lesson sources excluded
method: Compared exact source expression, example and meaning with all discovered canonical/selected/exploratory lesson titles, briefs and target detectors. A regex miss is not proof of distinct semantic ownership. Naturalness and seven-step transfer were reviewed qualitatively; conditional entries require a separate idiomaticity and pedagogical gate. No decision, draft, manifest, media or audit was changed.

candidates.sourceExpression: learning is caught rather than taught
candidates.exactSourceExample: At home, much learning is caught rather than taught.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Children absorb behaviour through observation; a catch metaphor.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Education maxim: observed behaviour learned without direct instruction; unlike 366/367 information uptake, the decision is whether modelling changes conduct.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Natural generalisation of the source maxim; fixedness needs editorial confirmation.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Compare adult modelling, peer norms, home routines, and explicit instruction; do not imply teaching is ineffective.

candidates.exactSourceExample: After a long shift, cooking seemed like another hurdle to get over.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Another difficulty to overcome; a fixed obstacle metaphor.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Canonical 1124 at the first hurdle marks the timing of a first obstacle; this source describes an additional task experienced as a difficulty to overcome.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Standard figurative hurdle construction; Cambridge defines a hurdle as a difficulty to overcome.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Decide whether a further task is a real obstacle, how to get over it, and when support reduces it.

candidates.sourceExpression: rewrite the story they were telling themselves
candidates.exactSourceExample: For the new pupil, a supportive class helped rewrite the story they were telling themselves.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Change a negative self-concept; a narrative metaphor.
candidates.proposedTargetUnit: rewrite the story you tell yourself
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Self-narrative revision based on new experience; not revision of a literal document or historical account.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Natural narrative metaphor; normalize pronouns and tense from the source.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Separate unsupported positive spin from an evidence-based revision of self-belief across school, work, sport.

candidates.exactSourceExample: After the break, the performers began to come back to themselves.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Recover their usual sense of balance or identity; a natural reflective phrase.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Regain ordinary balance or identity after disruption; canonical 1750 pulled themselves back from the brink requires near-serious failure and active rescue.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Natural reflective phrase, but review singular/plural reflexive agreement.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Distinguish simple rest from recovery of one’s usual self across performance, illness recovery, stress.

candidates.sourceExpression: a browser with too many tabs open
candidates.exactSourceExample: On busy days, my brain feels like a browser with too many tabs open.
candidates.sourceMeaning: A mind trying to handle too many thoughts at once; a digital simile.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Digital simile for competing thoughts; no current same-title or exact-source owner. Different from merely being busy: concurrent mental switching is central.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Contemporary figurative simile rather than a fixed dictionary idiom; teach as such.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Differentiate mental overload, actual browser tabs, task prioritisation, and when closing a thread helps.

candidates.exactSourceExample: A rumour can spread before the truth catches up.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Correct information eventually reaches people; a pursuit metaphor.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Correct information reaches the audience after a rumour; canonical 1521 catching up means friends exchanging recent news, not a delayed correction.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Natural pursuit metaphor; avoid promising that truth inevitably wins.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Contrast rumour lead versus verified correction; do not invent eventual vindication. Existing 1521 detector matches the source mechanically and must be narrowed first.

candidates.exactSourceExample: Those songs became emotional landmarks in her life.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Events or works that mark stages of feeling or memory; a map metaphor.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Songs/events serve as memorable reference points in a life, distinct from canonical 726 visual shorthand, where a sign conveys an idea quickly.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Defensible map metaphor, not an established fixed idiom; verify learner usefulness before drafting.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Choose when a memory anchors a period, rather than merely evoking a mood; transfer to places, films and rituals.

candidates.exactSourceExample: Even with a grant, the cost may bite.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Expenses may cause financial pain; a bite metaphor.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Expenses have a painful practical effect despite partial support; canonical 471 bite off more than you can chew concerns overcommitment, not financial impact.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: The source “the cost may bite” is compressed; prefer natural cost/costs + bite construction only after usage check.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Contrast felt cost after a grant versus mere sticker price; transfer to fees, repairs and ongoing bills.

candidates.exactSourceExample: Making soup can slow the day down.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Create a calmer pace; speed is figurative.
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: An activity changes the felt pace of a day; canonical 2252 slow down and reset is an explicit personal pause to regain clarity.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Natural verb phrase, but may be too compositional for a separate seven-step lesson.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Distinguish an unhurried routine from delay, inactivity, or a person deliberately pausing to reset.

candidates.sourceExpression: repair the roof while still living in the house
candidates.exactSourceExample: Transit planners must repair the roof while still living in the house.
candidates.sourceMeaning: Improve an active system without stopping daily use; a house metaphor.
candidates.proposedTargetUnit: repair the roof while still living in the house
candidates.whyNotSameSenseAlias: Improve an operating system without stopping its daily service; no matching selected source/detector owner found.
candidates.sourceNaturalness: Understandable extended analogy but may be a one-off image; only promote if a natural shorter reusable pattern is justified.
candidates.sevenStepTransferPotential: Differentiate live-service renovation from an offline rebuild; transfer to transit, a library, and a clinic.

excludedExamples.reason: draws a line around their time is likely a boundary variant of canonical 207 draw the line; do not open a new owner without a sense split.
all fireworks and not much substance is same core presentation-versus-value decision as selected 2961 more show than substance.
money is a good servant, but a poor master closely repeats selected 2457 a brilliant servant, but a poor master.
lean into has an existing same-sense active-engagement owner 1687.
cultural memory is already taught inside canonical 406; investigate alias expansion.
source uses tighten the screws for cinematic suspense, while the established idiom pressures a person to act; source-sense mismatch.

usageEvidence.note: Dictionary supports figurative obstacle to overcome.
Education paper uses the caught-versus-taught maxim as an observational-learning contrast.
Supports excluding suspense-only source use from the established coercive idiom.
